title: Fruit Into Baskets
description: Brute force to optimized: re-walking from every start versus a single coordinated variable-size sliding window tracking at most 2 distinct types.

blocks.text: You are visiting a row of fruit trees, represented by the array fruits, where fruits[i] is the type of fruit the i-th tree produces. You have exactly two baskets, and each basket can hold only a single type of fruit (but unlimited quantity of that type). Starting from any tree, walk to the right, picking exactly one fruit from every tree along the way, stopping the moment you'd need a third basket. Return the maximum total number of fruits you can pick this way.

blocks.caption: Grow the window; shrink it once a third fruit type appears

blocks.text: Given an array fruits representing the fruit type at each tree in a row, and exactly two baskets (each holding only one fruit type), find the maximum number of fruits collectible from any contiguous stretch of trees using at most 2 distinct fruit types.

blocks.title: Analogy: Picking Fruit With Only Two Baskets
blocks.text: Like walking down a row of fruit trees carrying exactly two baskets, one fruit type per basket, picking one fruit from every tree you pass, and having to stop the moment a third fruit type shows up because there's nowhere left to put it.

blocks.caption: Walk down the row picking fruit for two baskets, stopping the moment a third type appears

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","Result","Why"],"rows":[["The entire row [1,2,1]","only 2 distinct types (1 and 2)","Both baskets can hold everything here"],["Answer","3","All 3 trees can be picked using only 2 baskets"]]}

{"headers":["Step","Result","Why"],"rows":[["The stretch [2,3,2,2] (indices 1-4)","2 distinct types (2 and 3)","This is the longest stretch using only 2 fruit types"],["Answer","4","Starting from index 0 would require a third basket for the type at index 2"]]}

blocks.text: Edge case: every tree has the same fruit type
When the entire row is a single fruit type, only one basket is ever needed, and the whole row can be picked, giving an answer equal to the full length of fruits.
Before checking every possible starting tree and walking forward from scratch, notice this is really asking for the longest window containing at most 2 distinct values, a well-known shape.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: "At most 2 baskets, one fruit type each" is exactly the same as "at most 2 distinct values allowed in the window".

Observation 2: This is the exact same shape as Subarrays with K Different Integers's "at most k distinct" building block, just with k fixed at 2 and asking for the longest such window instead of counting them.

Observation 3: Grow a window from the right, tracking a frequency count of fruit types currently inside it. Whenever the window holds more than 2 distinct types, shrink from the left until it holds at most 2 again.

Observation 4: Track the maximum window length seen throughout this single coordinated pass.

Recognizing "at most k distinct values in a window" as a named, reusable pattern immediately suggests the variable-size sliding window with a frequency map, rather than needing to rediscover the technique from scratch.
This is a direct, k=2 special case of the more general "longest/count of windows with at most k distinct values" sliding window pattern.
For every possible starting tree, walk forward, adding fruit types to a set, stopping the moment a third distinct type would be needed.

items: For every possible starting tree, walk forward one tree at a time, tracking the set of distinct fruit types seen so far.
Stop extending the moment a third distinct type appears, and record the length of the stretch collected so far.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: A fresh set is built for every starting position, since each independent walk needs to track its own distinct types.
The inner walk breaks immediately once a third type would be needed, since continuing further from this same start could never produce a shorter, more useful result.
best only ever increases, tracking the single longest qualifying stretch found across every starting position.

blocks.text: Every possible starting position is checked directly, walking forward until a third type appears, so the correct maximum is always found.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n squared) in the worst case, since each of the n starting positions can walk forward up to n trees.
Space: O(1) extra, since at most 3 types are ever tracked in the set before stopping.
Limitation: restarting the walk and the type-tracking set from scratch at every new starting position ignores that a single coordinated sliding window can answer the same question in one linear pass.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: The brute force treats every starting tree independently, discarding useful information between them. Instead, grow a single window from the right, tracking a frequency map of fruit types currently inside it. Whenever the window holds more than 2 distinct types, shrink from the left until it holds at most 2 again. Since the left pointer only ever moves forward and never resets, the entire process runs in a single linear pass.

Maintain a window with a left and right boundary, along with a frequency map of fruit types in the window. Grow the window by advancing right. Whenever the frequency map holds more than 2 distinct keys, shrink from the left by removing trees until it holds at most 2 again. Track the maximum window length seen throughout.
Grow the window from the right, shrinking from the left only when a third distinct fruit type appears.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n), since left and right each advance forward at most n times total across the whole pass.
Space: O(1) extra, since the frequency map holds at most 3 entries at any moment (2 valid, plus the 1 that triggers a shrink).

The frequency map tracks exactly how many trees of each fruit type currently fall within the window. Its size (the count of distinct keys) exceeding 2 means a third type has appeared, and shrinking from the left removes trees (decrementing their counts, and removing a type entirely once its count reaches 0) until only 2 distinct types remain, at which point the window is valid again and can resume growing.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","What happens"],"rows":[["Window has at most 2 distinct fruit types","Keep growing the window by advancing right"],["Window has more than 2 distinct fruit types","Shrink from the left until only 2 distinct types remain"]]}

items: The frequency map is updated every time a tree enters the window (on growth) or leaves it (on shrink), always reflecting the window's current contents.
The shrink is a while loop, since more than one tree might need to be removed from the left before the window drops back down to at most 2 distinct types.
best is updated after any needed shrinking, always reflecting a currently-valid window's true length.

blocks.text: This problem is a direct, k=2 instance of the general "longest window with at most k distinct values" sliding window pattern, recognizable once the "2 baskets, 2 types" framing is translated into that language.

items: Not recognizing this as an "at most k distinct" problem, and instead trying to special-case exactly 2 types with ad-hoc tracking variables.
Shrinking the window by only one position instead of using a while loop, which can leave more than 2 distinct types in the window if multiple trees of the same leaving type needed removing.
Forgetting to remove a fruit type from the frequency map entirely once its count reaches 0, which would incorrectly inflate the distinct-type count.

items: Explicitly translate the "2 baskets" framing into "at most 2 distinct values", since recognizing the underlying pattern is the key step an interviewer is listening for.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: "Find the longest contiguous stretch using at most k distinct types/baskets/colors" points toward a variable-size sliding window with a frequency map, shrinking whenever the distinct count exceeds k.

items: How would this change if you had 3 baskets instead of 2? The exact same technique applies directly, just replacing the distinct-count limit of 2 with 3.

How would you count the total number of qualifying stretches, rather than find the longest one? This becomes the exact "at most k distinct" counting technique used in Subarrays with K Different Integers.
What if baskets had a maximum CAPACITY as well as a type restriction? An additional running count per type, compared against the capacity, would need to be tracked alongside the distinct-type count.
A direct, k=2 special case of the "at most k distinct values" technique used in Subarrays with K Different Integers.
Shares its variable-size sliding window shape with Longest Repeating Character Replacement and Minimum Size Subarray Sum, just with a different growth/shrink condition.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text:
Brute force: O(n squared) time, O(1) space.
Optimized (variable-size sliding window): O(n) time, O(1) space.

items: Pattern: Variable-size sliding window with a frequency map, the "at most k distinct values" pattern with k fixed at 2
Core Idea: Grow the window until a third distinct fruit type appears, then shrink from the left until only 2 remain
Time: O(n)
Space: O(1)
Most Important Observation: "2 baskets, one type each" translates directly into "at most 2 distinct values in the window", a well-known reusable pattern
Interview Difficulty: Medium
One-line memory trick: Grow until a 3rd type appears, then shrink from the left until only 2 remain
